checks: No eclipse at 4 of 21 covered epochs where the 2.45802 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 86498032 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 2.458 days and a primary eclipse depth of 0.78 percent dimming. No secondary eclipse was detected. The automated pipeline identified this system with a high detection significance of 156.0 in the box-least-squares search, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed a signal-to-noise peak of 18.8. However, two important caveats apply: alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true period is double what initial analysis found, though this correction does not affect the overall confirmation; additionally, the centroid offset of 6.9 arcseconds places this candidate very close to a brighter neighboring star, and TESS's resolution cannot confidently separate the two sources. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs.
